answer: Cast one ember probe per applicant: a quill-shaped sensor of unique alloy. The registry fires a heat pulse through it; the holder files the cooling echo, the decay curve of escaping heat. Each verified filing anneals the alloy, shifting the next expected curve, so readings chain to one holder alone. A replayed reading fails: no two alloys share a grain pattern, and a stale echo never matches the annealed curve. One probe runs $470 and 25 foundry hours; a farm wanting 5,000 fakes must forge 5,000 probes, $2.35 million and 125,000 hours, because each grain pattern is cast once and never repeats.
